Happening on Sun 16 Aug, the Stopford House Party is a brand-new festival set to take over the Brutalist square outside Stopford House. Visitors can expect live jazz from the Ted Branson Quartet, beer, wine and soft drinks from local favourites Runaway Brewery, delicious food from Aunty Lou’s and Stockport Provisions, and coffee from Stockport newcomers, HUSTLE. There’ll also be a series of workshops running throughout the day, including: Free drop-in badge-making with Local Press Club Free kite-making with Easy Peel Studio Urban sketching with Len Grant. ( Book tickets here) Free, guided photo walk with Steve Marland. The free-to-attend Stopford House Party will run from 12pm – 5pm. Alongside the parade and performances, Manchester Day promises family-friendly activities and lots of surprises, including the opportunity to step inside a giant whale, roaming puppets and brass bands. evidence_packet.evidence_text: A doctor who botched an operation so badly it was described as "not compatible with life" has been struck off the medical register Dr Yasser Adly Abdel Rahman, an NHS locum surgeon from Egypt, carried out the flawed emergency bowel procedure on a young man It meant the contents of the patient's bowel, leaving his stomach, were re-deposited back into his stomach through a circular "closed loop", the Medical Practitioners Tribunal Service (MPTS) heard The patient was left in "uncontrollable pain" and could have died but for another surgeon correcting the error in a second operation, the misconduct hearing, sitting in Manchester, was told Rahman at no time considered that something may have gone wrong surgically, the tribunal heard, despite the patient's parents and other medics expressing concerns A former consultant general and colorectal surgeon, acting as the General Medical Council's expert witness, said the procedure carried out by Dr Rahman was "not known to man" and his error was "as bad as it gets"

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Businesses, charities and community groups across Greater Manchester will soon be able to apply for a share of a new £20m fund aimed at improving local high streets Mayor Bev Craig announced the Good Growth High Streets Fund during a visit to Middleton town centre, saying she wanted people to feel the benefits of Greater Manchester's economic growth in the places where they live The fund is expected to open for applications later this year, although details of how much individual projects will be able to bid for have not yet been announced The mayor's office says the scheme could support a range of ideas to help town and district centres attract more visitors, including bringing empty shops back into use and supporting community events Craig said many residents were concerned by the decline of some high streets, pointing to boarded-up shops, derelict buildings and the loss of independent businesses "Our high streets are the beating hearts of our communities, and people want to feel pride about where they live," she said

evidence_packet.evidence_text: A cancer survivor who always dreamed of having children has opened up about the heartbreaking reality of going into surgical menopause at the age of 34 Gemma Coleman, who was diagnosed with two separate cancers affecting her ovary and womb in 2022, was told she would never be able to become pregnant after needing two major operations The 37-year-old, from Turton, Lancashire, said her diagnosis had "felt like a death sentence, but surviving cancer isn't the end of the story" as she now hopes to adopt in the future "You have to learn to live with the long-term physical and emotional impact of treatment," she said Gemma underwent two major operations, including the removal of her ovaries, womb, fallopian tubes, lymph nodes and affected abdominal tissue, followed by eight months of chemotherapy Now three years into remission, Gemma has regular scans and blood tests while managing the long-term effects of treatment including chronic pain, fatigue, bone weakness and fibrosis

Greater Manchester Fire and Rescue Service (GMFRS) said it was called to reports of a fire at Marc Darcy on Bury New Road in Salford at about 01:40 BST. The outlet was "well alight" when firefighters arrived and the blaze was tackled by eight fire crews and specialist units including a turntable ladder. A GMFRS spokeswoman said: "Crews remain in attendance as they continue to work to extinguish the fire and make the area safe." He said the business sold high-end men's designer suits and boasted several celebrities among their customers. evidence_packet.evidence_text: Sealing the deal: Summer resurfacing sees 21kms of new road surface laid down across Manchester | Manchester City Council Sealing the deal: Summer resurfacing sees 21kms of new road surface laid down across Manchester Thursday 13 August 2026 A huge programme of works is under way across Manchester to make sure our road network is in good condition as we head towards colder and wetter months. From the start of August through to the end of the month, highways crews will be out in force, carrying out surface dressing at nearly 30 locations across the city. Surface dressing is a cost-effective treatment that helps protect roads from everyday wear and tear. By sealing the road surface, it prevents water from entering small cracks and causing further deterioration. With the majority damage cause to the road surface during the winter months, work like this is vital to ensure the health of our road network, extending the life of our roads and reduce the need for more disruptive repairs in the future. Over the course of just two weeks, highways crews will treat approximately 154,000 square metres of road surface, covering more than 21 kilometres of carriageway across Manchester, roughly the distance from Manchester city centre to Glossop. The programme also incorporates the use of recycled granite chippings as part of Manchester City Council's commitment to more sustainable highway maintenance. Some of the roads included in this year's programme are: Alan Turing Way Wythenshawe Road Princess Road Yew Tree Road Barlow Moor Road For a full list of roads included in the programme visit out website here. evidence_packet.evidence_text: Bury The 137 ‘leaky dams’ installed high on the moors, and the problem they might solve The structures use natural techniques to retain more rainwater on the hills Comments News Chris Gee Local democracy reporter 09:39, 02 Aug 2026 View 2 Images 137 d A massive natural flood management project in and around Holcombe Hill is seeing 137 wooden dams currently being built to ‘slow the flow’ of water The National Trust and United Utilities (UU) have joined forces on a project which aims to ease water inflows during intense wet weather and improve water quality in the River Irwell and its tributaries, by using natural techniques to retain more rainwater on the hills and moors Led by contractors Aitch Conservation, work has started on the installation of 137 ‘leaky dams’ across the Stubbins Estate, managed by the National Trust The dams aim to capture high-velocity water run-off from intense rainfall, which is then stored temporarily before gradually being released, reducing the risk of flooding further downstream The trust said the intervention is an extension of previous restoration works to mitigate climate change, support farming and improve habitats across our moor, farms and woodland areas

The figures come as Andy Burnham pledged to cut the number of jobless young people He made the commitment as he unveiled plans to open up new technical education routes to 14-year-olds, which will be put on an equal footing with traditional academic pathways. News Todd Fitzgerald Executive editor 17:55, 31 Jul 2026 Upda The death of a man detained in Salford is being investigated by the police watchdog. Ricky Swindells, 28, was dealt with by officers last Friday (July 24) after they attended a property on Duchy Road following a 999 call A report of concern for Mr Swindells' welfare was made, the Independent Office for Police Conduct (IOPC) said. During the call, at around 7.40pm, his family said he was autistic and in 'significant distress' Police handcuffed Mr Swindells to restrain him, the IOPC added. Body worn camera footage shows officers saying that was done for his own safety, the watchdog said Mr Swindells then became unresponsive, the IOPC said, before receiving treatment at the scene. Officers began CPR at 8pm and paramedics arrived seven minutes later, the watchdog added. Officers gave CPR before North West Ambulance Service personnel took over, the IOPC said Mr Swindells was taken to hospital, where he died the next day, Saturday, July 25. Greater Manchester Police said it is supporting the investigation. The force said Mr Swindells was 'restrained by officers responding to a report by family members of a man in crisis'

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Salford Family of man who died after being handcuffed by police following 999 call 'devastated', solicitor says as IOPC probe continues Ricky Swindells died last week. An Independent Office for Police Conduct (IOPC) probe is underway. News Todd Fitzge The family of a man who died after being handcuffed by police following a 999 call are 'devastated', their solicitor said as a watchdog investigation continued Ricky Swindells, 28, was restrained by officers last Friday (July 24) after they attended a property on Duchy Road, Salford. A report of concern for Mr Swindells' welfare was made, the Independent Office for Police Conduct (IOPC) said. During the call, at around 7.40pm, his famil Police handcuffed Mr Swindells. Body worn camera footage shows officers saying that was done for his own safety, the watchdog said Mr Swindells then became unresponsive, the IOPC said, before receiving treatment at the scene. Officers began CPR at 8pm and paramedics arrived seven minutes later, the watchdog added. Officers gave CPR before North West Ambulance Service personnel took over Mr Swindells was taken to hospital, where he died the next day, Saturday, July 25. Greater Manchester Police said it is supporting the investigation. The force said Mr Swindells was 'restrained by officers responding to a report by family members of a man in crisis'

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Courts Florist handed driving ban after cutting corner and knocking 70-year-old into the air The victim sustained broken bones and spent eight days in hospital Comments News Greta Simpson Senior Reporter 13:57, 19 Aug 2026 View Image The junction of G A florist has been handed a driving ban after committing a 'careless and unsafe' manoeuvre which put a 70-year-old man in hospital for eight days Adele Shaw-Frost, 40, was behind the wheel of a white Kia Sportage on the evening of January 6 this year when she 'cut a corner' and collided with John Hogan on Penmore Close in Shaw, Minshull Street Crown Court heard today (August 19) Mr Hogan had been at the Morning Star pub in Shaw and was walking home along Grains Road with his grandson on what was said to be a dark and wet evening with snow on the ground He reached the junction with Penmore Close, less than 100ft from the pub, and began to cross the road, prosecutor Simon Barrett told the court "Ms Shaw-Frost turned right into the road in what we say was a rushed manoeuvre. evidence_packet.evidence_text: Courts Four men on trial accused of murdering Alexander John Soyoye, 16, amid 'clash with rival gang' fled UK in wake of killing, jurors told Ruben Candiza, Valdo De-Almeida, Marco Veiga and Emerson Teta deny murdering Alexander John Soyoye News Amy W Four men on trial accused of murdering a 16-year-old boy amid a 'clash with a rival gang' fled the country in the wake of the killing, a jury has heard Alexander John Soyoye, also known as John, lost his life on November 5, 2020. It came, jurors heard, amid a feud between the Moston based 'M40' gang and the Rochdale and Oldham outfit Representing the Danger (RTD). Prosecutors said hostilities spilled onto the streets of Moston Manchester Crown Court heard the stabbing of a relative of an M40 gang member in Piccadilly Gardens earlier that day was the catalyst for a brutal 'revenge' attack which resulted in Mr Soyoye's death hours later Jurors heard RTD members later headed to Moston to 'exact revenge', with the groups involved in a violent melee. M40 gang members became overwhelmed and fled, it was said Mr Soyoye was injured in the earlier fight, jurors heard. He became isolated before being punched, kicked and stabbed, the court heard, suffering 15 blows to his body. Mr Soyoye, the trial heard, died at the scene

He was just 16 It followed a feud between Moston based 'M40' gang and the Rochdale and Oldham outfit Representing the Danger (RTD). Hostilities spilled out onto the streets, with 21 young men said to have been involved in total. Three weeks into the trial, and as their defence cases were due to begin, the four men changed their pleas to guilt Six members of the RTD gang were previously convicted of John’s murder and sentenced in 2022. The crackdown was launched amid 'persistent' reports of anti-social behaviour, drug-related crime and the exploitation of vulnerable residents on the Thornbank Estate As part of the operation, two closure orders were issued in the area as three further addresses were also closed through 'tenancy action or voluntary surrender'. A new Urban Care and Neighbourhood (UCAN) centre was also opened in the centre of the estate Over the last 15 months, police said the number of incidents reported has halved and crime volume has reduced by almost 30 per cent. A police chief said the estate has been 'transformed' during the crackdown The operation, between GMP, Bolton Council and Be One Homes, came to an end this week. Sergeant Oliver Cooper, from GMP's Neighbourhood Team in Bolton said: "This operation has been significant in increasing public confidence and safety

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Droylsden Iconic Droyslden landmark set to be torn down The Concord Suite has jutted out of the Droylsden skyline since the 1970s Comments News George Lythgoe Local Democracy Reporter 17:01, 04 Aug 2026 Updated 17:01, 04 Aug 2026 View 2 Images Droylsd After dominating the Droylsden skyline for half a century, the Concord Suite is being partially torn down The iconic building, in the heart of the Tameside town, was built in the early 1970s and served as a base for the now defunct Droylsden Council. It was also a venue for weddings, community events and dances in its heyday. Now it sits empty and lifeless Tameside council has lodged a planning application to partially demolish the Concord Suite as part of plans to bring new life to the site and support the wider regeneration of the town centre The proposed works would demolish the upper parts of the building, including the former function room and dance hall, while retaining the lower levels and securing the remaining structure. The lower levels have been earmarked for redevelopment for housing, retail and leisure This is the latest step in the progression of the Droylsden Masterplan. The local authority says this project will create new opportunities for residents, businesses and visitors while strengthening the town centre for future generations

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Real Life 'Sight loss won't stop me climbing a 4,221m mountain in the Swiss Alps' Lucy Hobson could become the first woman with sight loss to reach its summit News Rachael Davis, PA and Stephen Topping Senior reporter 06:05, 03 Aug 2026 Updated 06:41, A Stockport mountaineer could become the first woman with sight loss to reach the summit of a huge Swiss Alps mountain. Lucy Hobson, 33, will tackle Zinalrothorn later this month The 4,221-metre peak was first climbed in 1864, but Lucy is looking to make history when she tackles the mountain. Lucy has optic atrophy, a genetic condition where the optic nerves shrivel rather than form, which causes permanent vision loss While her condition has worsened over the years, Lucy refuses to let it stand in her way. "When I started doing these kinds of challenges, it was just for myself, really," she said "It is what I enjoyed, and it is what made me happy. I always suffered a lot with depression, and this helps me a lot "And then, aiming a bit higher... (I can) show people that if I can do it, if you're thinking about wanting to do something and there's something stopping you, just go and do it. Because once you take that first step, you'll never look back."

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Tameside He lured her to her death and left a grieving family without closure Alisha Apostoloff-Boyarin was preyed upon and murdered - but the man responsible has never said where he left her View 5 Images Alisha Apostoloff-Boyarin was killed by a vio News Stephen Topping Senior reporter 07:34, 22 Aug 2026 Ripped apart from their 'lovely girl' by a twisted, remorseless killer, Alisha Apostoloff-Boyarin's family have suffered heartache upon heartache. The 24-year-old was reported missing by her grandmother on February 2, 2022 She was one of the people Alisha was closest to in her young life, with the pair having spent a period of time living together. But she had not heard from Alisha in a couple of weeks and was growing concerned about her Greater Manchester Police issued a public missing person's appeal to try and find Alisha on March 1, 2022. Later that month, the search became a murder investigation, as detectives came to the sad conclusion Alisha had 'come to serious harm' I spoke to Alisha's grandmother outside her Ashton-under-Lyne home in the days following GMP's announcement. She was in shock at the events that were unfolding around her and clearly worried sick about her beloved granddaughter She was also determined to do what she could to try and bring her beloved granddaughter home. She was keen to speak to the Manchester Evening News as part of this, but at the moment we spoke she was expecting a GMP officer to arrive any minute with an update about Alisha

The footage of his arrest has now been published by police Ashley Crowder, 37, murdered popular musician and former DJ Graham Cox , 37, in March 2024, after subjecting him to 'prolonged cruelty', Bolton Crown Court heard Before eventually murdering him, Mr Crowder 'dominated and exploited' Mr Cox , repeatedly attacking him and stealing his benefits A video clip has been released by Greater Manchester Police which shows the moment officers attended the scene. Body cam footage shows Crowder the door, saying his 'mate has passed away' and beckoning police inside Shortly after, Mr Crowder can be seen sitting in the back of a police van. He told cops: "What it is... my mate's passed away, I was just going to ring the ambulance, then... do you wanna come up?"

The female defendants also received money from associates of the brothers. Their relationships did not become sexual and they did not smuggle contraband on the Nawaz's behal Gascoyne admitted being in an inappropriate relationship with Dil Nawaz between January 20, 2024, and April 4, 2024. evidence_packet.evidence_text: Courts 'My school shared a wall with a prison - I knew what I needed to do' Steve Duffy specialises in lending support to those leaving prison after long and complex sentences News Amy Walker Court reporter 07:37, 25 Jul 2026 View Image Steve Duffy (I A probation officer whose school was beside a prison says it sparked an interest in helping people rebuild their lives Steve Duffy - based in Greater Manchester - said that as kids' footballs sailed over into the jail, he quickly realised prisoners were doing 'the exact same thing' on the other side It motivated him to want to make a difference to people's lives. He now specialises in the Offender Personality Disorder (OPD) pathway, supporting those leaving prison, many after long or complex sentences. Steve helps them reintegrate into the community and build more stable liv The OPD pathway is a national partnership between NHS England and HM Prison and Probation Service. It provides specialist psychological support for people in the justice system with complex personality and mental health needs, helping manage risk and reduce reoffending Steve said: "My primary school shared a wall with a prison, so criminal justice always felt very present to me from a young age. I remember footballs being kicked over the wall and thinking 'we're doing the exact same thing on either side'

She has been classed as a 'high-risk' missing person, with multiple appeals to find her issued in recent days GMP has now shared two images showing what Jessica was wearing on July 16, including a black zip-up top, while she could also be seen carrying one bag on the bus and two in the first CCTV image. New technology telling passengers what stops are coming up was one of the many upgrades brought to Greater Manchester when it But calls are growing for northern accents to replace the neutral automated sounds which keep bus passengers updated every day It’s not just buses either, at Manchester Piccadilly train station an automated voice using what seems to be received pronunciation - also known as King's English - is often what keeps commuters updated. They said the plan would not meet density requirements of 35 homes per Officers acknowledged there were some ‘constraints’ on parts of the site, including trees and the fact the M66 runs alongside it. However, they said they had ‘no evidence’ regarding which areas of the land would not be developable They added building smaller homes or terrace housing could be a way to increase density, even with the constraints Officers did not, however, reject the principle of having housing on the green belt land. Manchester Crown Court heard how Kaelun Howe, 22, burgled - and attempted to burgle - numerous premises in the days leading up to the robbery at the bookie In April this year, he turned up at a man's house and pointed a gun at him through the peephole. "I'm going to shoot you," he said Later that afternoon, Howe forced his way into the William Hill at Salford precinct, armed with what appeared to be a gun, but turned out to be a BB gun. The cashier moved into a safe room behind glass before Howe shot at it He then climbed onto the counter and stole the contents of the till His terrifying attacks ended when he was arrested at Manchester Airport. Howe has now been jailed for six years and nine months for a string of burglary and robbery offences

Eight strike dates were called at Ravensfield and Lily Lane primary schools in January Teaching union NASUWT claimed that a 'culture of violence and intimidation' had led to frequent attacks on staff. It said that both pupil-on-teacher and pupil-on pupil assaults had 'grown to untenable levels' The union blamed leadership at both schools and the multi-academy trust which runs them. Changing Lives in Collaboration (CLIC), the trust which runs both schools, insisted that the allegations made 'did not reflect the day-to-day reality' at either academy It was a row that grabbed national headlines. Striking staff had the support of Manchester Evening News readers commenting on social media, and several parents of both current and former pupils at the two primary schools who spoke to the MEN It was just the beginning of a turbulent seven-month period for the two CLIC Trust schools. The day before the 44-year-old had been found guilty of sex offences following a trial at Manchester Crown Court and remanded to prison awaiting sentence It was his first time in jail and he was classified by staff as a 'vulnerable prisoner' who was 'significantly vulnerable to assault', a report by the Prisons and Probation Ombudsman (PPO) said. Her treatment for ovarian and womb cancer triggered an immediate surgical menopause, meaning she would never be able to become pregnant Now, Gemma, from Turton, Lancashire, is backing research that could result in better treatment options for one of the most aggressive forms of ovarian cancer The research, led by The University of Manchester , has been fuelled by a new £2.5m Cancer Research UK Grant. evidence_packet.evidence_text: Press release — 14 August 2026 14:39 Share Share this story Copy link Link copied! Download Our new Bury NeighbourHub brings help with training and employment, life skills and wellbeing support closer to local people The new Neighbourhub is now open In the Millgate shopping centre, having moved from its previous location and expanded its offer It gives residents the opportunities to learn new skills, improve their confidence, get online and access help into work, making it easier to improve their prospects and build a brighter future The Bury NeighbourHub is a key part of Greater Manchester's Live Well approach, making it easier for residents to access joined-up support, skills, employment and wellbeing services in one convenient community location. The Peveril of the Peak – or simply The Pev, to most of us – had just been named the best pub in the UK earlier this week. The Pev has now assured fans that the pub will remain in the Swanick family, even without Nancy at its helm. ADVERTISEMENT “With love, The Swanicks.” RIP to a true local legend.
